name: ky
notes: Case: a library with one long README (about 45 KB) and no other documentation. Ground truth = README changes between v2.0.0 and v2.1.0 that the v2.1.0 code supports, checked in source/. Left out: FAQ additions, security warnings about forwarding credentials (advice, not behaviour), example header values, link additions and the clarification of ky.create. The empty first/last progress chunk was already wrong in v2.0.0 code; the maintainers fixed the text in v2.1.0.

items.what: There is a ky.query(input, options?) shortcut for the QUERY method.
QUERY is one of the standard methods that are uppercased.
The default retry methods include query.

items.anchor: If `maxRetryAfter` is set to `undefined`, it will use `options.timeout`.
items.what: maxRetryAfter defaults to Infinity (not undefined/options.timeout); a retry timing delay larger than maxRetryAfter is capped to maxRetryAfter.

items.anchor: If `retry` is a number, it will be used as `limit`
items.what: retry.limit, including the numeric shorthand, must be a finite, non-negative integer (otherwise an error is thrown).

items.anchor: If the response provides an HTTP status contained in `afterStatusCodes`
items.what: 413 is only retried when the response has a retry timing header; besides RateLimit-Reset the headers X-RateLimit-Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset and X-Rate-Limit-Reset are used as fallbacks.

items.anchor: Also, `.json()` throws if the body is empty or the response status is `204`.
items.what: .json() throws on an empty body unless the parseJson option handles empty bodies (parseJson receives the text).

items.anchor: Per-attempt timeout in milliseconds for getting a response, applied independently to each retry.
items.what: Ky shortcut methods also use timeout as a separate timeout for reading the response body; such body timeouts are not retried by retryOnTimeout.

items.anchor: data that was sent. Note: It's empty for the first call.
items.what: onDownloadProgress: the chunk contains the received data; there is no empty first call (an empty chunk only when an empty body completes).

items.anchor: data that was sent. Note: It's empty for the last call.
items.what: onUploadProgress: the last call carries the final chunk; an empty chunk only when an empty request body completes.
When extending an instance, signals are combined; replaceOption(signal) replaces inherited signals, signal: undefined removes them.

items.anchor: population is bounded by the request timeout and a 10 MiB response body size limit
items.what: error.data reads are bounded by the timeout or 10 seconds when timeout is disabled and by the remaining totalTimeout; if totalTimeout expires, a TimeoutError is thrown instead of HTTPError.
Highlights: upload and download progress and response validation with Standard Schema are features.
